newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ag attache revises up India cotton forecast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ag attache revises up India cotton forecast.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache pegged India 1995/96 cotton production at 12.3 million 480 lb bales, or 15.7 million 170 kg (375 lb) bales, well above prior forecasts and higher than official U.S. and Indian estimates.

Last week, India's Cotton Advisory board (CAB) revised up its estimate of 1995/96 cotton output to a record 15.6 million 170 kg bales. The U.S. Agriculture Department has estimated India cotton production at 11.9 million 480 lb bales.
The attache said the output forecast was revised up "based on the record market arrivals and considering the fresh estimates as reckoned by various sources."
In a report dated August 30, the attache said the jump in 1995/96 production was due to good rainfall in the central zone during January and February which much improved yields.
Area under cotton also went up to 8.65 million hectares from 7.86 million hectares in 1994/95, the attache noted.
The attache previously pegged 1995/96 India cotton output at 11.9 million 480 lb bales.

The attache also revised up a forecast for 1996/97 cotton production to 11.3 million 480 lb bales from 10.5 million bales, saying the revival of monsoon activity during August in the major cotton producing states brightened crop prospects after a dry spell.
The new estimate is above 10.5 million bales forecast by USDA in its Aug. 12 World Supply and Demand report.
